analysis:
All four units are documentation only (hardware-support.md, inference.md). No executable code changed, so no control regressed directly. Material security-relevant claims in the diff:
1. The GLM5-Next weight-hash change (inference.md head 684-691) replaces separate pre- and post-load WeightHasher passes with the manifest aggregate verified during load. In coordinator mode it is then cached via VerifiedWeightHashStore and keyed on file stat identity (device, inode, size, mtime, ctime). The cached hash is registered without rereading weights. Integration should check the real code in ProviderLoop.verifiedGLM5NextWeightHash and VerifiedWeightHashStore. It should confirm that the TOCTOU window between per-file hashing and construction is closed, that stat identity is sufficient against T-012/T-027 operator tampering, and that the store itself is not user-writable (cache poisoning). That code is not in this batch, so I treat it as an unverified contract. I recorded only a low-severity threat-model gap, not a code defect.
2. New output-control refusal (`EngineV2Bridge.nativeOutputControlRefusal`) returns a 400 before reservation. This looks availability-positive, since it avoids striking the inference-error breaker (T-010 area). It is not verified in code.
3. GLM response_format and strict tools are validated after generation, with output withheld until validation passes. The text describes fail-closed behavior (422 with no content). This is consistent with T-008 and is unverified here.
4. The video frame-timing change (variable-frame-rate now accepted) widens the media-parsing surface. The decoded-frame cap of 512 MiB remains documented, which is a bounded mitigation.
5. The hardware-support.md memory-availability formula (`reclaimable`) counts page cache and purgeable pages, which could over-admit loads. That is an availability and memory-pressure matter and is not verified in code.
The inference.md base_text unit covers only unchanged lines 1-415 and does not touch the diffed regions.

findings.detail: The inference.md patch (head lines 684-691) documents that coordinator-mode registration will publish a cached manifest aggregate (`GLM5NextManagedLoad.verifiedArtifactSHA256`, `VerifiedWeightHashStore`) without reading the weights. It will skip the read while each file's device, inode, size, mtime and ctime are unchanged. This is a documentation-only change, so it is not a code regression. It does create an attack surface that T-012 (operator replaces model weights) and T-027 (weight substitution) do not describe. An operator with write access could modify weight bytes in place and then restore mtime. ctime cannot be set from userland, but a replace-and-rename or a write that evades the identity check could still be a gap. The load "verifies again before serving", which narrows the window, but the registered hash is not itself freshly verified. The threat model should record this trust assumption and its limits.
findings.title: Docs now say the GLM5-Next weight hash is the manifest aggregate, with later starts skipping a weight read (T-012 / T-027 / T-034 assumptions)
